fixes.explanation: Paul, the man writing this letter, asks them to be "…like-minded, having the same love, being united in spirit and purpose." That's a whole team pulling the same direction. Picture a crew of cookie boxes stacked on a shelf, all lined up facing the same way instead of each one sliding off in its own direction. That's the kind of unity he's after.

Worry is a real struggle for plenty of people, but Paul doesn't name it in verse 3. He says, "Do nothing out of selfish ambition or empty pride…" Those two are about how we treat each other. Worry about tomorrow is a different batch, and Paul isn't mixing it in here.

That pair sounds like it belongs in the verse, I'll give you that. But Paul's two are "…selfish ambition or empty pride…" Selfish ambition is chasing your own gain, and empty pride is puffing yourself up. Anger and jealousy are real troubles too, but they aren't the two he lists in verse 3.

Paul writes that He "…humbled Himself and became obedient to death—even death on a cross." That's as low as the road goes. The Son who existed in the form of God went all the way down to a cross. Paul wants the believers in Philippi to see how far humility can reach.

A battlefield makes sense if you picture a hero's story, but verse 8 says something else. Paul writes, "…became obedient to death—even death on a cross." The word is cross, not battlefield. Obedient is the word Paul uses for Him.

Paul writes, "Therefore God exalted Him to the highest place and gave Him the name above all names…" He humbled Himself all the way down, and God lifted Him all the way up. That little word "Therefore" is the hinge. The humbling came first, and the lifting follows from it.

Paul writes, "But even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I am glad and rejoice with all of you." Glad is the first word of the pair. He says it even if he is poured out like a drink offering. That's a lot of gladness from a man in a hard spot.

Paul doesn't say afraid in verse 17. He writes, "…I am glad and rejoice with all of you." Those two words are what he says even if he is being poured out like a drink offering. Fear isn't part of the verse.
